counterparty: US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware
stated_reason_verbatim: on November 10, 2014, Dendreon Corporation (the 'Company') and its wholly owned subsidiaries ... filed voluntary petitions for relief (the 'Chapter 11 Filings') under Chapter 11 of Title 11 of the United States Code ... On November 10, 2014, the Company received a Staff Delisting Determination letter from the Listing Qualifications Staff of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC
source_doc: Dendreon 8-K (Items 1.03 and 3.01), 2014-11-12
notes: Case No. 14-12515 (PJW); assets sold through a court-supervised process (bidding procedures order 2014-12-19).

event_title: Valeant acquires substantially all Dendreon assets out of bankruptcy for USD 495m
stated_reason_verbatim: the Purchaser agreed to acquire substantially all of the assets and certain liabilities of the Debtors (the 'Sale Transaction') for an aggregate purchase price of $495 million (which includes the purchase of $80 million in cash and the Debtors' assets related to their enteric coated D-3263 hydrochloride product candidate), of which $445.5 million is payable in cash at closing and $49.5 million is payable in common shares of Valeant
source_doc: Dendreon 8-K (Item 7.01), 2015-02-20
notes: Second amended and restated acquisition agreement dated 2015-02-19; closed in Q1 2015 (Valeant Q1 2015 investor presentation lists Dendreon among 'acquisitions closed in Q1').

event_title: EU marketing authorisation for Provenge withdrawn at Dendreon's request
stated_reason_verbatim: On 6 May 2015, the European Commission withdrew the marketing authorisation for Provenge ... The withdrawal was at the request of the marketing authorisation holder, Dendreon UK Ltd, which notified the European Commission of its decision to permanently discontinue the marketing of the product for commercial reasons.
source_doc: EMA EPAR page, Provenge, 'Withdrawn' status and overview
notes: EU authorisation granted 2013-09-06; no European revenue was ever disclosed.

event_title: Valeant sells Dendreon to Sanpower Group for USD 819.9m cash
stated_reason_verbatim: VALEANT TO SELL DENDREON TO SANPOWER GROUP FOR $819.9 MILLION IN CASH ... its affiliate has entered into a definitive agreement to sell all of the outstanding equity interests in Dendreon
source_doc: Valeant 8-K Ex-99.1 press release (2017-01-10)
notes: Closed mid-2017 (Valeant 10-K FY2016 describes the agreement; completion date not read). After closing Provenge revenue is no longer publicly reported.

event_title: uniQure will not seek renewal of Glybera's EU marketing authorisation; authorisation expires October 2017
stated_reason_verbatim: 'The decision to not pursue marketing authorization renewal of Glybera in Europe involved a thoughtful and careful evaluation of patient needs and the clinical use of the therapy, and is not related to any risk-benefit concern,' stated Matthew Kapusta, chief executive officer of uniQure. 'Glybera's usage has been extremely limited and we do not envision patient demand increasing materially in the years ahead.'
source_doc: uniQure 8-K Ex-99.1, 'uniQure Announces It Will Not Seek Marketing Authorization Renewal for Glybera in Europe' (2017-04-20)
notes: Intramuscular AAV1. EMA: 'The marketing authorisation for Glybera (alipogene tiparvovec) expired on 28 October 2017 ... uniQure biopharma B.V. confirmed that it did not apply for renewal of the authorisation due to the lack of demand for this product' (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/glybera). uniQure also terminated the Chiesi commercialisation agreement (10-Q Q1 2017).

event_title: GSK transfers its rare disease gene therapy portfolio (incl. Strimvelis and OTL-200) to Orchard Therapeutics
stated_reason_verbatim: In April 2018, we entered into the GSK Agreement, pursuant to which GSK transferred its portfolio of approved and investigational rare disease gene therapies to us, which included Strimvelis and OTL-200 for MLD, among other programs. GSK also simultaneously novated to us their R&D Agreement with Telethon-OSR.
source_doc: Orchard Therapeutics 10-K FY2022 (filed 2023-03-14), License agreements; Orchard F-1 (2018-10-04)
notes: Manufacturing model: gammaretroviral ex vivo. Day of month (12 April 2018) taken from the public announcement and not re-verified in the filings read, which say 'April 2018'. Consideration: GSK took a 19.9% equity stake plus royalties (per F-1; amount not stated in USD). F-1: 'Since receiving marketing authorization, only a limited number of patients have been treated with Strimvelis' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1748907/000119312518293354/d566761df1.htm).

event_title: Orchard discontinues investment in Strimvelis and other primary immunodeficiency programmes and seeks alternatives
stated_reason_verbatim: Orchard intends to discontinue its investment in and seek alternatives for its programs in rare primary immune deficiencies. These include OTL-103 for the treatment of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS), OTL-102 for X-linked chronic granulomatous disease (X-CGD) and Strimvelis, a gammaretroviral vector-based gene therapy approved in Europe for adenosine deaminase severe combined immunodeficiency (ADA-SCID).
source_doc: Orchard Therapeutics 8-K Ex-99.1, strategic update (2022-03-30)
notes: Part of a 30% workforce reduction. Strimvelis product sales were USD 0.6m in Q2 2022.

event_title: Strimvelis marketing authorisation transferred from Orchard to Fondazione Telethon (non-profit)
stated_reason_verbatim: In July 2023, the marketing authorization for Strimvelis was transferred to Fondazione Telethon, a non-profit organization ... upon formal approval by the European Commission. As marketing authorization holder, Fondazione Telethon will assume the outstanding obligations relating to the program, and we will no longer receive revenue from sales of or incur costs associated with Strimvelis. ... The marketing authorization for Strimvelis was transferred to Fondazione Telethon on July 17, 2023
source_doc: Orchard Therapeutics 10-Q for quarter ended 2023-09-30 (filed 2023-11-13)
notes: No consideration disclosed (transfer to the academic originator). EMA EPAR page now lists Fondazione Telethon ETS as MAH (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/strimvelis).

event_title: EU conditional marketing authorisation for Zalmoxis withdrawn at MolMed's request
stated_reason_verbatim: On 9 October 2019, the European Commission withdrew the marketing authorisation for Zalmoxis (nalotimagene carmaleucel) in the European Union (EU). The withdrawal was at the request of the marketing authorisation holder, MolMed S.p.A, which notified the European Commission of its decision to permanently discontinue the marketing of the product for commercial reasons.
source_doc: EMA EPAR page, Zalmoxis, 'Withdrawn' status and overview
notes: Manufacturing model: allogeneic gene-modified T cells (HSV-TK). Conditional authorisation from 2016-08-18, renewed yearly; withdrawal followed the failed TK008 confirmatory trial. MolMed press release not retrieved (company later acquired by AGC, 2020).

event_title: Takeda records JPY 74.0bn impairment on Alofisel after ADMIRE-CD II failure
stated_reason_verbatim: The JPY 119.3 billion impairment losses recorded in the current period primarily includes JPY 74.0 billion impairment charges for ALOFISEL (for complex Crohn's perianal fistulas) following topline results of phase 3 ADMIRE-CD II trial
source_doc: Takeda 6-K, FY2023 Q3 (nine months to 2023-12-31) financial results (2024-02-02)
notes: Amount in JPY (c. USD 0.5bn at early-2024 rates; not converted in the amount field). ADMIRE-CD II topline 2023-10-17: study 'did not meet its primary endpoint of combined remission at 24 weeks' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1395064/000139506423000129/alofiseltoplineresults.htm).

event_title: Takeda voluntarily withdraws Alofisel's EU marketing authorisation
stated_reason_verbatim: 'Those valuable discussions indicated that despite the conflicting results across our data, the clinical benefit of Alofisel is no longer sufficient to justify its continued use in the EU. We recognize the difficulty of this outcome for patients and will work closely with the Crohn's Perianal Fistulas (CPF) community during this transition.' (Ramona Sequeira, Takeda)
source_doc: Takeda statement, 'Takeda Provides an Update on Alofisel (darvadstrocel)' (2024-12-13); EMA EPAR page, Alofisel
notes: EMA: 'On 13 December 2024, the European Commission withdrew the marketing authorisation for Alofisel ... at the request of the marketing authorisation holder, Takeda Pharma A/S, which notified the European Commission of its decision to permanently stop the marketing of the product in the EU' (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/alofisel). Takeda: 'engaging health authorities about this outcome in countries where Alofisel is currently approved' (Japan).

event_title: Takeda discontinues all cell therapy research and seeks external partner for its platform
stated_reason_verbatim: Takeda (TSE:4502/NYSE:TAK) today announced that as part of a strategic portfolio prioritization process, the company has made the decision to discontinue its cell therapy efforts. Takeda will seek an external partner to leverage its cell therapy platform technologies
source_doc: Takeda 6-K, statement 'Takeda Provides Update on Cell Therapy Research' (2025-10-01)
notes: Ten months after the Alofisel EU withdrawal. Trade press (Fierce Biotech) reports 137 US roles affected and an expected impairment of c. JPY 58bn on the gamma-delta platform; not verified from the 6-K read. Takeda statement page: https://www.takeda.com/newsroom/statements/2025/takeda-provides-update-on-cell-therapy-research/

event_title: Atara licenses tab-cel (Ebvallo) commercialisation in Europe and other ex-US markets to Pierre Fabre
stated_reason_verbatim: Pierre Fabre will pay the Company an upfront cash payment of $45 million for the exclusive license grant. The Company is also entitled to receive an aggregate of up to $318 million in milestone payments upon achieving certain regulatory and commercial milestones relating to the Product.
source_doc: Atara 8-K (Item 1.01), Commercialization Agreement with Pierre Fabre Medicament effective 2021-10-02 (filed 2021-10-04)
notes: Predates EU authorisation (2022-12-16) by 14 months; Pierre Fabre is the EU marketing authorisation holder. Manufacturing model: allogeneic EBV-specific T cells (off-the-shelf).

event_title: Atara out-licenses remaining global (incl. US) tab-cel rights, manufacturing and development to Pierre Fabre; associated Atara restructuring
stated_reason_verbatim: Pierre Fabre Laboratories to License Commercialization Rights to Tab-cel, including Regulatory, Manufacturing and Development Activities, in the United States and All Remaining Markets. Atara to Receive Additional Payments of up to USD 640 Million, Significant Double-digit Tiered Royalties as a Percentage of Net Sales, and Funding of Tab-cel Global Development Costs. Tab-cel Global Partnership and Associated Strategic Restructuring Extends Atara Cash Runway into Q3 2025
source_doc: Atara 8-K Ex-99.1, 'Atara Biotherapeutics Announces Expanded Global Tab-cel Partnership with Pierre Fabre Laboratories' (2023-11-01)
notes: Amount is the maximum additional consideration. Closing announced 2024-01-08 with 'Focused Operational Activities and Associated Strategic Restructuring' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1604464/000119312524003945/d703405dex992.htm).

event_title: Atara cuts c.50% of workforce and pauses CAR-T programmes after FDA complete response letter for Ebvallo BLA; strategic review
stated_reason_verbatim: Atara remains focused on delivering on the future financial value of EBVALLO and has paused ATA3219 and ATA3431 CAR-T programs and implemented a workforce reduction of approximately 50% to preserve resources. Strategic review by financial advisor ongoing
source_doc: Atara 8-K Ex-99.1, Q4/FY2024 results (2025-03-07)
notes: CRL issued January 2025 on third-party manufacturing GMP observations; BLA resubmitted 2025-07-14 (PDUFA 2026-01-10). Q1 2025: Atara 'expects to reduce its operating expenses year-over-year by approximately 65% in 2025'.

event_title: Atara transfers all worldwide tab-cel manufacturing and supply responsibility (and later BLA sponsorship) to Pierre Fabre
stated_reason_verbatim: In March 2025, the Company completed the transfer of all worldwide manufacturing and supply responsibility, including all associated costs, to Pierre Fabre Laboratories, and the Company is in active discussions on accelerating the transfer of all remaining operational activities related to tab-cel to Pierre Fabre, except the BLA sponsorship
notes: Q3 2025 release (2025-11-12): 'Atara has completed the transfer of substantially all tab-cel activities, including BLA sponsorship, and associated costs to Pierre Fabre Laboratories' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1604464/000119312525276209/d66575dex991.htm). Originator fully exits operations; retains royalties and a USD 40m approval milestone.
